approved: Treasury Laws Amendment (Combating Illegal Phoenixing) Bill 2019
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that targets illegal phoenixing, where company assets are sold off to avoid paying creditors.
It would create new criminal and civil offences for directors and others who carry out or help with deals that strip a company of property and defeat creditors.
One new strict liability offence would apply to anyone who fails to obey an order from the corporate regulator to return property obtained through such a deal.
Introduces new offences for creditor-defeating dispositions of company property.
Penalises those who engage in or facilitate such dispositions.
Allows liquidators and the corporate regulator to recover the property.
Company officers, persons who facilitate property dispositions, and liquidators and the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC).
Treasury Laws Amendment (Combating Illegal Phoenixing) Bill 2019 - Consideration in Detail - Director ID numbers
Treasury Laws Amendment (Combating Illegal Phoenixing) Bill 2019 - Third Reading - Suspend the usual procedural rules

The speaker argued the Treasury Laws Amendment (Combating Illegal Phoenixing) Bill 2019 does not go far enough to address phoenixing, which costs the Australian economy $2.9–$5.1 billion annually, and announced Labor will introduce amendments to implement director identification numbers and a five-year review. The speech cited cases of Tara Teo and Ian Campbell of JUMP! Swim Schools, and noted Professor Helen Anderson’s view that the bill alone will not solve the problem.

The speaker welcomed the government's acceptance of their amendments to the Treasury Laws Amendment (Combating Illegal Phoenixing) Bill 2019, but expressed scepticism that the bill's measures would be sufficient. They highlighted the importance of director identification numbers to track recidivist directors who defraud creditors and the Australian Tax Office, and urged the government to expedite related legislation.
